Fairly promising demo. Combat has some JRPG feels while the overall exploration and atmosphere creates a similar tone to Trials of Fire, travelling through an unforgiving desert with little green inbetween. Being in a fight has a nice tactical feel, and feels good in general, though combat could be rounded out with some more enemy variety (and, skills for each enemy to use. They're fairly low on variation what a single lad can do to you, at least currently) Some mechanics at the moment do feel like they need some more time cooking (movement costs / health loss / the resulting "economy" / resource manament). For example, you can move further purely using your health, than you can on your full supply stores, even after fully upgrading your capacity. I've mentioned this and some more in the feedback to the demo, and there's a lot of time for the developers to consider where to take things from there. There's also a few bugs, most being fairly minor, but alas this can be expected from such an early version. In the end, with some care, some thoughts on existing concepts, and additions to make playthroughs varied (characters, more foes, more abilities, more sidegrades to abilities, most of which seem already planned), this has the potential to be a really fun Roguelite.

Love the style and feels great, but gameplay is most important and the gameplay doesn't promote having fun. - You can't trade in the city or replenish health/supplies. - Managing supplies and inventory weight requires too much micromanagement (since you can't go back to the city to dump trade items..) - Doesn't promote exploring because of how taxing taking a single step is to supplies. You move 6 hexes and you're out of supplies. One stash you find gives you enough to take two steps, and you need 10-15 to find the next stash.

This is a fun little turn based RPG rogue-like with a hunger mechanism which makes the game about hopping from resource to resource, and hoping you find relief in time when you cross the deserts. Unfortunately, in this prequel, I have pretty well played it out in under 10 hours.. given that, I am a bit concerned about how many maps the full version will have, and what the continuance of characters between maps will be.. hopefully there's some dynamic generation so that the play-ability can continue somewhat indefinitely. This demo is definitely worth playing, with the sole exception that it is frustrating when you realize that you've maxed out your game, but the full version isn't available yet.. unless you're reading this after it's been released ;-)

Sandwalkers is a very promising exploration title; I'm excited for the full release! Currently, my biggest complaints are supplies or food availability on the map. Even with efficient management, food stocks run out quickly and you seldom have an opportunity to replenish it outside of the green tiles. The snail character also tends to overshadow the rest of the party with its defense and attacks, especially when it has more levels. I love the unique style of the game the combines well with the interesting story and combat elements.

This game is really cool and I want to enjoy it, but the experience has been soured by bugs and poor quality control. In the 1.5 hours I've played, I've had to force close from task manager 4 times. Some have been gameplay bugs, and some resolution issues. I've seen a number of other things such as; programming code showing up where text is supposed to be for quests/dialog/tooltips, text being in the wrong language, character health showing up as ♥♥♥♥♥♥ and messing up the UI, mysteriously taking damage after attacking when there's no status to explain it, etc. Really, the game seems awesome and fresh. I wanted to play out everything the prologue has to offer, but this an unreasonable amount of problems for what could be an excellent demo. I hope it's fixed and I can come back to enjoy it after some time.

I was very excited about this game and had it on my radar for a long time. The idea is unique, but the execution is not there. This is a rogue-like game and the difficulty was expected. However, the early game is a death sentence. Supplies are always low or non-existent. Combats are tedious and difficult. I've experienced taking damage for no reason at all which is especially frustrating. There are status effects (thorns and poison) that cause characters to take damage, but having none of these statuses on your character and still taking damage is extremely annoying. Your only chance early game is to walk around the main area hoping to get ambushed so you can farm encounters. If you don't do this there is no hope as your caravan won't make it out of the desert without dying from an ambush or lack of supplies. You can unlock memories during your runs that can unlock permanent upgrades for future caravans. However, this makes all of your early runs meaningless and makes it hard to get attached to the game since it is impossible to go after the main mission. Basically, your first runs are just fodder so you can unlock memories. I don't think that mechanic is very fun and turned me away from the game about an hour in. Make combats more forgiving early on. Maybe have enemies slightly scale with the more memories you earn? I don't know, but the early game is not fun at all. Make supplies more readily available. If you roll dry weather, you're screwed. Not fun. Basically, the game has a cool idea that is squandered by the mechanics. I wouldn't recommend it in it's current state.

There seems to be potential for a great game somewhere in here, but it's unplayable in its current state. Clearly, time has been spent crafting the world, the story, the lore... it's just a shame it's all presented in a way that is unintuitive, cumbersome and frustrating to the point where I couldn't be bothered struggling with it beyond an hour or so. The game needs a major UX overhaul.
